title: Machine-learning pipeline identifies antimicrobial hexapeptides
summary: A sequential machine-learning pipeline screened virtual libraries of 6–9-residue peptides and identified three leading antimicrobial hexapeptides. The paper reports activity against multidrug-resistant clinical isolates and therapeutic effects in a mouse bacterial-pneumonia model. These are laboratory and animal results, not clinical efficacy.
ai_technology: Sequential machine-learning pipeline for peptide selection, classification, ranking and activity regression

source_review.scope: Primary Nature indexed article text and PubMed abstract/metadata/affiliation record for the ML hexapeptide screening study, its January 2023 publication date and reported mouse pneumonia assays.

evidence.tested: The authors report a sequential machine-learning pipeline over virtual 6–9 amino-acid sequence space; the leading three identified hexapeptides were tested against clinical multidrug-resistant isolates and in a mouse bacterial-pneumonia model.
evidence.unknown: The mouse model and reported comparison with penicillin do not establish human efficacy. The PubMed primary metadata gives journal online date 2023-01-12; no earlier pre-2020 version is identified in the reviewed primary material.
evidence.ai_role: Sequential learned modules selected, classified, ranked and regressed peptide candidates from the virtual sequence library; the reported three lead hexapeptides are outputs of that workflow.
